title: Object properties by id
introduction: An object layer stores objects as a dict keyed by the object ids placed in the editor, so the id is the lookup. The parsed entry carries position (area), the tileset reference (ttype, variant), and the authoring properties.
code:
from tilemap_parser import load_map

data = load_map("data/map.json")
layer = data.get_layer("Objects")
obj = layer.objects[7]          # dict[int, ParsedObject]; the key is the oid

assert obj.ttype == 0
assert obj.properties["pickup"] == "coin"
assert (obj.area.x, obj.area.y, obj.area.w, obj.area.h) == (8, 24, 16, 16)

# iterate all objects together with their ids
for oid, entry in layer.objects.items():
    assert entry.area.w >= 0

title: Properties of a placed tile
introduction: Tiles placed on a tile layer can carry properties. Access is by cell coordinates; the returned ParsedTile can be None outside the layer's placement.
code:
from tilemap_parser import load_map

data = load_map("data/map.json")
tile = data.get_tile_at("Terrain", 1, 0)   # (name or id, cell_x, cell_y)
assert tile is not None
assert tile.properties["surface"] == "ice"
assert tile.ttype == 0 and tile.variant == 0

title: Layer lookup by name or id
introduction: Layers are addressable by name (str) and by id (int). The list helpers filter by layer type and visibility.
code:
from tilemap_parser import load_map

data = load_map("data/map.json")

named = data.get_layer("Terrain")            # by name
listed = data.get_layers(layer_type="tile")  # only tile layers
assert named is not None
assert named in listed

visible_only = data.get_layers(include_hidden=False)

title: Surface for one placed object
introduction: The loader cuts each object's surface from its tileset sheet. The result is a (surface, screen_x, screen_y) tuple, already positioned in world pixels.
code:
from tilemap_parser import load_map

data = load_map("data/map.json")
result = data.get_object_surface_by_id("Objects", 7)
assert result is not None

surface, screen_x, screen_y = result
assert surface.get_size() == (16, 16)
assert (screen_x, screen_y) == (8, 24)

title: Custom properties on a collision tile
introduction: The tileset collision file may carry custom properties per tile beyond layer and mask. Parsing keeps them verbatim on TileCollisionData; they are the natural home for per-tile behavior markers.
code:
from tilemap_parser import CollisionCache

cache = CollisionCache()
ts = cache.get_tileset_collision("data/collision/ground.collision.json")

tile = ts.tiles[0]                  # keyed by the collision file's tile id
assert tile.properties["surface"] == "gear"
assert tile.collision_layer == 1
assert len(tile.shapes) == 1

title: Tile data at a cell in a PhysicsWorld
introduction: A world stores stacked (gid, flip) entries per cell. tile_ids_at lists the stored gids, resolve_collision resolves the collision data for one gid, and the collision data follows any movement result through ground_tile_id.
code:
from tilemap_parser import CollisionCache, PhysicsWorld, load_map

cache = CollisionCache()
ts = cache.get_tileset_collision("data/collision/ground.collision.json")
data = load_map("data/map.json")

cell_map = data.build_tile_map()            # {(col, row): ((gid, flags), ...)}
world = PhysicsWorld(cell_map, ts, tile_size=(16, 16))

assert 0 in world.tile_ids_at((1, 0))       # gids stored at that cell
tile = world.resolve_collision(0)           # TileCollisionData | None
assert tile is not None
assert tile.properties["surface"] == "gear"
